key_finding: Gaussian processes are the canonical nonparametric Bayesian model. They place a prior directly over function space, and the kernel encodes all inductive bias — smoothness, periodicity, length-scale. The posterior is exact (conjugate Gaussian), producing calibrated uncertainty at every query point. Sparse GPs use variational inference with inducing points to scale from O(n^3) to O(nm^2), closing the trilogy: info theory (KL as objective) → Bayes (posterior as target) → VI (ELBO as method) → GPs (unifying application).
